summary: In the county zoning jurisdiction in unincorporated Boone County, the ordinance pauses the filing, processing, review or acceptance of data-center applications. Its stated term runs June 16, 2026 through June 15, 2027. The definition excludes on-campus facilities providing internal IT to that business.
trigger: Covered application during the stated moratorium

evidence: tanked water brought to site in bulk
summary: For data centers subject to the county ordinance, cooling water must be brought to the site in bulk and managed in a closed non-evaporating loop. Local wells, town water and surface water cannot be used for cooling.

evidence: Small-scale server rooms accessory to another permitted use
summary: The data-center definition excludes small-scale server rooms accessory to another permitted use. The infrastructure tests for data centers therefore should not be automatically applied to those rooms.

County rules call for closed-loop water circulation to cool processing equipment. Applicants can propose another design if they demonstrate to the commissioners that it uses both less water and less energy than a closed-loop system.

evidence: every two (2) years after operations commence
summary: Applicants submit a water feasibility study at filing. If the project relies on nonpublic water sources, it also supplies that study to the county every two years after operations begin.
trigger: Nonpublic water supply for recurring study

evidence: prohibit data centers in any of the City's zoning districts
summary: The adopted June amendment prohibits data centers in all city zoning districts. Check separately for an existing approval or vested project; this city-district finding is not a rule for all unincorporated land in the ETJ.

locator: City caption of Ordinance 2026-04; zoning ordinance 99-08, §§2.21–2.22
evidence: PERMISSIBLE USE BY CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT
summary: Within Talty zoning jurisdiction, the city added data centers to its use chart as permissible by conditional use permit. The published caption does not identify the eligible district(s); do not infer that every district is eligible.

locator: Ordinance 0847-26-ORD, §2, Exhibit VII.2-3-4, p. 4; June 15 adoption confirmed by city notice
summary: The nonresidential use table requires a special use permit in Light Industrial, Warehouse and Heavy Industrial districts for a data center listed as an accessory or warehouse/storage use. The city confirms residential districts prohibit it.

evidence: as a principal use unless approved in a
summary: A principal data center requires an explicit specific plan or amendment adopted through rezoning. A plan can cover only a specified part of its area; check the mapped plan and any approved conditions.

evidence: The Marana water department will not provide potable water
summary: Marana Water will not supply potable water to principal or accessory data centers for cooling, humidity control and similar uses. The developer must document another water source; this is not a prohibition on all domestic water service.

locator: Ordinance 5957 §2, Table 11-7-2, note 18; confirmed by city September 2025 bulletin
evidence: ONLY IF SPECIFICALLY AUTHORIZED BY CITY COUNCIL
summary: Under the city employment table a principal data center in GI or HI requires specific council authorization at Planned Area Development overlay approval. Separate provisions govern accessory uses and existing vested sites.
The data-center parking minimum is one space per 5,000 square feet for the first 200,000 square feet and one per 10,000 square feet thereafter.
trigger: First 200,000 square feet versus incremental area above 200,000

locator: July 27 meeting memo (Current Definitions + Proposed Changes) paired with confirmed adoption of Ordinance 3965; Ch. 118
summary: At 10,000 square feet or less, a new data center may be approved by council special use permit in C-1, C-2, I-1 or I-2. Inclusion in an industrial district is not by-right approval.

locator: July 27 meeting memo (Current Definitions + Proposed Changes) paired with confirmed adoption of Ordinance 3965; Ch. 118
summary: A new data center larger than 10,000 square feet may be approved by council special use permit in C-2, I-1 or I-2. The general category does not include C-1.
